about: The held-pose rule (A11): src/domain/orientation/orientation.ts classify() and track(), and HeldPose.classify and PoseTracker (Kotlin), pass every row and every track; JS ignores side. g is gravity in g; physical null is the dead band. side is native's alone: left is the phone's top to the left (gravity along +x, ROTATION_90), right the other way round (ROTATION_270), a hypothesis until the device gate reads the encoded picture upright both ways round (P4). The edge rows are the nearest readings either side of each comparison, as V8's Math.hypot and atan2 compute them (HeldPose.kt computes them the same way): 60 and 30 degrees exactly cannot be reached by any reading, so their rows are the readings one step either side. holdMs is HOLD_MS on both sides. Each track starts from nothing settled; settled and side are the tracker's settled reading after each step. Change only with both.

edge: one step under 0.87 (0.8699999999999999) is held upright

tracks.why: a reading settles at exactly holdMs, not a millisecond before
a dip into the dead band restarts the hold: it runs from the reading after the dip
a swing through the dead band to upright settles upright after its own hold
turning to the other side: JS stays landscape, native settles the new side after the hold
laid flat after being held sideways
no gravity is a reading that settles unknown, unlike the dead band
the dead band alone never settles anything
